title: Lirazine Accelerates Cardiomyocyte Proliferation in Cryoinjured Zebrafish Ventricle
main_claim: Lirazine raised the EdU positive cardiomyocyte index from 4.1 percent in controls to 7.6 percent in treated animals, an increase of 85 percent.
excerpt: Lirazine raised the EdU positive cardiomyocyte index from 4.1 percent in controls to 7.6 percent in treated animals, an increase of 85 percent.

title: Pooled Reanalysis of Lirazine Studies in Zebrafish Cardiac Regeneration
main_claim: Across the pooled set lirazine raised the proliferating cardiomyocyte index by 71 percent relative to matched controls.
excerpt: Across the pooled set lirazine raised the proliferating cardiomyocyte index by 71 percent relative to matched controls.

title: No Detectable Effect of Low Dose Lirazine at Three Days After Cryoinjury
main_claim: Low-dose lirazine (10 µM) did not affect cardiomyocyte proliferation or scar area at 3 days post-cryoinjury in zebrafish.
excerpt: The proliferating cardiomyocyte index was 1.9 percent in controls and 2.0 percent in treated fish, a difference of 0.1 percentage points that is well inside the variation we see between clutches.

title: Dose Response of Lirazine in the Cryoinjured Zebrafish Heart
main_claim: The dose response is therefore steep and late, which is consistent with reports of an effect at high concentration and with null reports at 10 micromolar.
excerpt: The dose response is therefore steep and late, which is consistent with reports of an effect at high concentration and with null reports at 10 micromolar.

title: A Compartment Model of Border Zone Cardiomyocyte Cycling Under Lirazine
main_claim: The model predicts that lirazine increases the proliferating cardiomyocyte index from 4.3% to 7.1% at 7 days post injury.
excerpt: The simulations predict a clear effect on the proliferating cardiomyocyte index, rising from 4.3 percent to 7.1 percent at 7 days post injury in the median draw.

title: Thermal Cycling Durability of Copper Exchanged Zeolite Cu-MZL-8 for Ammonia SCR
main_claim: Increasing copper loading in Cu-MZL-8 leads to higher initial activity but greater loss of conversion and surface area after thermal cycling, indicating reduced durability.
excerpt: Surface area fell by 11 percent at the highest loading and by 3 percent at the middle loading.

title: Hydrothermal Aging Versus Dry Cycling in Copper Zeolite NOx Catalysts
main_claim: The two aging routes therefore do not produce the same catalyst, and a soak only protocol would have passed a material that fails in the regime cycling exposes.
excerpt: The two aging routes therefore do not produce the same catalyst, and a soak only protocol would have passed a material that fails in the regime cycling exposes.

title: Density Functional Study of Copper Site Migration in Small Pore Zeolites
main_claim: The computed barrier for migration of an isolated copper ion out of its six ring site is 1.78 electron volts in the dry cell and 1.12 electron volts with two water molecules present, a reduction of 37 percent.
excerpt: The computed barrier for migration of an isolated copper ion out of its six ring site is 1.78 electron volts in the dry cell and 1.12 electron volts with two water molecules present, a reduction of 37 percent.

title: A Survey of Stability Claims for Copper Zeolite NOx Reduction Catalysts
main_claim: Reported conversion retention after aging ranged from 41 to 98 percent, and the spread narrows substantially once protocol is accounted for.
excerpt: Reported conversion retention after aging ranged from 41 to 98 percent, and the spread narrows substantially once protocol is accounted for.

title: Combined Measurement and Kinetic Modeling of Conversion Loss Under Thermal Cycling
main_claim: A single pathway is therefore sufficient to explain the curve, and no second mechanism needs to be invoked.
excerpt: A single pathway is therefore sufficient to explain the curve, and no second mechanism needs to be invoked.

title: A GPU Shallow Water Solver for Urban Flood Simulation at Neighborhood Scale
main_claim: On a 16 million cell domain at 3 meter resolution the solver sustained 2.1 billion cell updates per second, which simulates 6 hours of flood evolution in 94 seconds of wall clock time.
excerpt: On a 16 million cell domain at 3 meter resolution the solver sustained 2.1 billion cell updates per second, which simulates 6 hours of flood evolution in 94 seconds of wall clock time.

title: Validating a GPU Flood Solver Against Stream Gauge and Depth Sensor Records
main_claim: The GPU shallow water solver predicted road flood depths with a mean absolute error of 7.3 cm and slightly underpredicted depth, while gauge‑only validation would overstate accuracy by about 40 % and residuals were four times more sensitive to drain capacity than surface roughness.
excerpt: Simulated peak depth matched sensor records with a mean absolute error of 7.3 centimeters and a bias of negative 2.1 centimeters, meaning the solver slightly underpredicted depth on roads.

title: Stability and Error Behavior of a Well Balanced Scheme for Wetting and Drying Fronts
main_claim: Truncation error in smooth wet regions is second order in grid spacing and reduces to first order within a band of roughly one cell width around the front, which yields an observed convergence rate of about 1.7 for problems containing a moving shoreline.
excerpt: Truncation error in smooth wet regions is second order in grid spacing and reduces to first order within a band of roughly one cell width around the front, which yields an observed convergence rate of about 1.7 for problems containing a moving shoreline.

title: How County Emergency Managers Interpret and Use Flood Model Output
main_claim: Managers treated any shaded cell as impassable, rejected uncertainty displays, and valued earlier delivery over higher resolution.
excerpt: Managers described uncertainty bands as something they could not put in front of a sheriff, and 15 of 23 said they would crop or simplify a map before sharing it.

title: Benchmarking Four Variant Calling Pipelines on Simulated and Reference Genomes
main_claim: The reversal in ordering of pipelines on insertions and deletions between reference samples and simulated data shows that at least part of the apparent advantage on reference samples is specific to those samples.
excerpt: The ordering of pipelines on insertions and deletions reversed between reference samples and simulated data for 2 of the 4 pipelines, which indicates that at least part of the apparent advantage on reference samples is specific to those samples.

title: Teaching Computational Reproducibility in a Graduate Engineering Course
main_claim: Artifact scores improved substantially, with the share of submissions that a second person could rerun rising from 21% to 79% and concept inventory scores increasing from a mean of 9.4 to 13.8 of 18 items.
excerpt: The share of submissions that a second person could rerun from the repository alone rose from 21 percent at the start of the module to 79 percent at the end.
